home.title: Your Site Name — Your Tagline
home.description: A short description of your homepage for search engines and social sharing. Keep it between 120 and 160 characters.

hero.title: A base template for consistent interfaces, not another kit of identical cards.
hero.lead: Fern UI is the starting point for your next projects: color and typography tokens already defined, ready-to-use components, dark mode included by default.

i18n.heading: Two languages, ready from the start
i18n.description: Every string in the app routes through useI18n() — locale files are the single source of truth, English and Italian side by side, out of the box.
i18n.hint: Switch language from the toggle in the header to see this whole page update live.

buttons.heading: Clear actions, for every context
buttons.description: Four semantic variants and three sizes, covering everything from toolbar actions to the main call to action.

badges.heading: Status and selection at a glance
badges.description: Badges communicate a non-interactive status; chips are selectable or removable, useful for filters and tags.

cards.heading: Containers with hierarchy, not all the same
cards.description: Three different treatments based on content weight: a feature card, a numeric one and a compact list.

feature.title: Design system ready
feature.paragraph: Colors, typography and spacing come from the same tokens, in light and dark mode, without redefining them for every component.

accordion.heading: Frequently asked questions about the starter
accordion.description: Expandable panels with height animation and persistent open state.

theme-colors.title: How do I change the theme colors?
theme-colors.content: Edit the variables in theme.css: every component reads them automatically, both in light and dark mode.

nuxt-compat.title: Do the components work with Nuxt 4?
nuxt-compat.content: Yes, every component is a Vue Single File Component with no external dependencies besides Tailwind v4.

dark-mode.title: Can I disable dark mode?
dark-mode.content: Yes, just don't apply the .dark class to the html element: components stay in the light theme.

form.heading: Every control a form needs
form.description: Text, textarea, select, checkbox, radio and switch, with consistent focus and error states.
form.accept-terms: I accept the terms of service

dialog.heading: Confirmations that don't break the flow
dialog.description: Title and actions scale with the dialog's own size prop, from a small confirmation to a full-height panel.

sm.title: Delete this project?
sm.content: This action is permanent: all associated files and settings will be lost.

md.title: Invite a teammate
md.subtitle: They'll get an email invite
md.content: Add a teammate by email to give them access to this project. You can change their role at any time from the settings page.

lg.title: What's new in v2.6
lg.subtitle: Release notes
lg.content: This release adds four new form components (switch, radio, select, badge), a semantic radius scale, and a full internationalization panel on the homepage. See the changelog for the full list of fixes.

full.title: Terms of Service
full.subtitle: Please review before continuing
full.content: This starter template is provided as-is, for use in personal and commercial projects. You are free to modify, extend and redistribute it as part of your own work. No warranty is provided — see the repository license for the full terms.

components.heading: Built for real content
components.description: Beyond buttons and forms — a media carousel for galleries and a sanitized rich text renderer for CMS-sourced content.
components.rich-text-intro: BaseRichText converts a block array into sanitized HTML, styled with the same typography tokens as the rest of the app — safe to use directly with CMS content.
components.rich-text-list-item-2: Ordered and unordered lists, quotes and code blocks

responsive.heading: Looks right on every screen
responsive.description: The same tokens and components adapt from phone to desktop, with no separate breakpoints to maintain by hand.

footer.made-with: Designed and developed with ❤ by Stefano Biddau
